Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-6382", "title": "Kidney Tests", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "They are fist-sized organs on either side of your backbone above your waist."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Your kidneys filter and clean your blood, taking out waste products and making urine."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Kidney tests check to see how well your kidneys are working."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "They include blood, urine , and imaging tests."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Early kidney disease usually does not have signs or symptoms."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Testing is the only way to know how your kidneys are doing."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "It is important for you to get checked for kidney disease if you have the key risk factors - diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease, or a family history of kidney failure."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Specific kidney tests include: Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) - one of the most common blood tests to check for chronic kidney disease ."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "It tells how well your kidneys are filtering."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Creatinine blood and urine tests - check the levels of creatinine, a waste product that your kidneys remove from your blood Albumin urine test - checks for albumin, a protein that can pass into the urine if the kidneys are damaged Imaging tests, such as an ultrasound - provide pictures of the kidneys."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The pictures help the health care provider see the size and shape of the kidneys, and check for anything unusual."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Kidney biopsy - a procedure that involves taking a small piece of kidney tissue for examination with a microscope."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "It checks for the cause of kidney disease and how damaged your kidneys are."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-3536", "title": "Homelessness and Health", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Each night, hundreds of thousands of people experience homelessness in the United States."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Some of these people experience chronic homelessness, while others have temporarily lost their shelter."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The reasons why they are homelessness are complex."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "They can include a combination of factors such as: Poverty Unemployment Lack of affordable housing Mental and substance use disorders Trauma and violence Intimate partner violence Justice-system involvement Sudden serious illness Divorce Death of a partner or parent Disabilities What is the link between homelessness and health?"}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Poor health can contribute to homelessness."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "And being homeless can contribute to poor health."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Many of the problems that people experiencing homelessness face can make their health worse, including: Limited access to health care Problems getting enough food Trouble staying safe Violence Stress Unsanitary living conditions Exposure to severe weather What are some of the common health problems that people experiencing homelessness have?"}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Some of the common health problems that people experiencing homelessness may have include: HIV Lung diseases , including bronchitis , tuberculosis , and pneumonia Malnutrition Mental health problems Substance use problems Wounds and skin infections Many people experiencing homelessness are dealing with trauma."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "This includes children, who are at risk for emotional and behavioral problems ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Contact your local homelessness assistance agency to get the help you need, such as access to shelters, health centers, and free meals."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1597", "title": "Healthy Living", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Healthy living means taking care of your body and mind by making choices that support your overall wellbeing."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Some you can't control, like your genetic makeup or your age."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "But there are many daily habits you can change to help you feel your best."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Creating new healthy habits takes time, but small, steady changes are easier to maintain and can become part of your everyday routine."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Healthy living can help you feel better, boost your energy, and lower your risk for serious health problems such as heart disease, cancer, and stroke."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "What steps can I take toward healthy living?"}, {"id": "S006", "text": "You don't have to change everything at once."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Start with a few steps to build a foundation for a healthier lifestyle."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "These can include: Get the screening tests recommended for you, including those specific to women's health and men's health Stay up to date on vaccines to protect yourself from disease Maintain a healthy weight that's right for you Eat a variety of healthy foods , and limit calories, added sugar, and saturated fat Be physically active , even small amounts of exercise can be helpful Keep your blood pressure and cholesterol in a healthy range Don't smoke , or take steps to quit if you do Protect your skin from too much sun Limit alcohol , or choose not to drink at all Get enough sleep each night to help your body and mind recharge Manage stress and work on improving your mental health , such as by practicing meditation, relaxation techniques, or gratitude Protect yourself from sexually transmitted infections (STIs) Visit your health care provider regularly for checkups See your dentist and eye care specialist for routine care Stay connected with friends, family, or community groups, and do activities you enjoy Healthy living is a lifelong journey."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Over time, small steps can add up to big health benefits."}]}, {"id": "MLP-464", "title": "Cancer Chemotherapy", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Cancer chemotherapy is a type of cancer treatment."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It uses medicines to destroy cancer cells."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Normally, your body forms new cells as needed, replacing old cells that die."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Cancer cells keep growing without control."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "New cells grow even when you don't need them, and old cells don't die when they should."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "These extra cells can form a mass called a tumor."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Chemotherapy works by killing the cancer cells, stopping them from spreading, or slowing their growth."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Chemotherapy is used to: Treat cancer by curing the cancer, lessening the chance it will return, or stopping or slowing its growth."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Ease cancer symptoms by shrinking tumors that are causing pain and other problems."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "What are the side effects of chemotherapy?"}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Chemotherapy does not just destroy cancer cells."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "It can also harm some healthy cells, which causes side effects."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "You may have a lot of side effects, some side effects, or none at all."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "It depends on the type and amount of chemotherapy you get and how your body reacts."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Some common side effects are: Mouth sores Fatigue Nausea and vomiting Pain Hair loss There are ways to prevent or control some side effects."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Talk with your health care provider about how to manage them."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Healthy cells usually recover after chemotherapy is over, so most side effects go away over time."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "What can I expect when getting chemotherapy?"}, {"id": "S018", "text": "You may get chemotherapy in a hospital, at home, at your provider's office, or a medical clinic."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "You might be given the medicines by mouth, in a shot, as a cream, through a catheter (a thin tube), or intravenously (by IV)."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Your treatment plan will depend on the type of cancer you have, which chemotherapy medicines are used, the treatment goals, and how your body responds to the medicines."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Chemotherapy may be given alone or with other treatments."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "You may get treatment every day, every week, or every month."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "You may have breaks between treatments so that your body has a chance to build new healthy cells."}]}, {"id": "MLP-5987", "title": "Chronic Kidney Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "You have two kidneys, each about the size of your fist."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They remove wastes and extra water, which become urine."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "They also keep the body's chemicals balanced, help control blood pressure, and make hormones."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Chronic kidney disease (CKD) means that your kidneys are damaged and can't filter blood as they should."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "This damage can cause wastes to build up in your body."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It can also cause other problems that can harm your health."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Diabetes and high blood pressure are the most common causes of CKD."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The kidney damage occurs slowly over many years."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Many people don't have any symptoms until their kidney disease is very advanced."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Blood and urine tests are the only way to know if you have kidney disease."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Treatments cannot cure kidney disease, but they may slow kidney disease."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "They include medicines to lower blood pressure , control blood sugar , and lower cholesterol ."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Sometimes it can lead to kidney failure ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "If your kidneys fail, you will need dialysis or a kidney transplantation ."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "You can take steps to keep your kidneys healthier longer: Choose foods with less salt (sodium) Control your blood pressure ; your health care provider can tell you what your blood pressure should be Keep your blood sugar in the target range, if you have diabetes Limit the amount of alcohol you drink Choose foods that are healthy for your heart: fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy foods Lose weight if you are overweight Be physically active Don't smoke NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}]
